name: Compiler Design
description: Lexical analysis, parsing, syntax-directed translation, intermediate code, runtime environments and code optimisation.

nodes.name: Compiler phases
nodes.desc: The phases of a compiler, what each produces and which errors each catches.
nodes.summary: You will be able to name the phases of a compiler, state what each one produces and identify which errors each phase catches.
topics: Intermediate code, optimisation and code generation

nodes.name: Lexical analysis
nodes.desc: Tokens, lexemes and patterns; a lexer as a finite automaton built from regular expressions.
nodes.summary: You will be able to describe tokens, lexemes and patterns and explain how a lexer is built as a finite automaton from regular expressions.
topics: From regular expressions to NFA and DFA

nodes.name: Counting tokens
nodes.desc: Longest match, lookahead, counting tokens in a program and lexical errors.
nodes.summary: You will be able to count the tokens in a program using longest-match and lookahead rules and recognise lexical errors.

nodes.name: Symbol table
nodes.desc: What the symbol table stores, how it is organised and which phases use it.
nodes.summary: You will be able to explain what a symbol table stores, how it is organised and which compiler phases read or update it.
topics: Phases that use the symbol table

nodes.name: Parsing
nodes.desc: The parser's job, parse trees and derivations, and top-down versus bottom-up parsing.
nodes.summary: You will be able to build parse trees and derivations for a grammar and contrast top-down with bottom-up parsing.

nodes.name: Grammar rewriting
nodes.desc: Ambiguity and the dangling else, eliminating left recursion and left factoring.
nodes.summary: You will be able to detect ambiguous grammars, resolve the dangling else and rewrite grammars by removing left recursion and left factoring.

nodes.name: FIRST & FOLLOW
nodes.desc: Computing FIRST and FOLLOW sets.
nodes.summary: You will be able to compute FIRST and FOLLOW sets for every non-terminal of a context-free grammar.
topics: End marker in FOLLOW of start symbol
FIRST of a string of symbols

nodes.name: LL(1) parsing
nodes.desc: Recursive descent, LL(1) tables and testing whether a grammar is LL(1).
nodes.summary: You will be able to write recursive descent parsers, build LL(1) parsing tables and test whether a grammar is LL(1).

nodes.name: LR parsing
nodes.desc: Shift-reduce parsing with handles, and shift-reduce and reduce-reduce conflicts.
nodes.summary: You will be able to run shift-reduce parsing using handles and identify shift-reduce and reduce-reduce conflicts.

nodes.name: LR(0) & SLR
nodes.desc: LR(0) items, the canonical collection and SLR(1) tables.
nodes.summary: You will be able to construct LR(0) items and the canonical collection and build LR(0) and SLR(1) parsing tables.

nodes.name: CLR & LALR
nodes.desc: LR(1) items, canonical LR and LALR tables, and how the parser classes compare.
nodes.summary: You will be able to build canonical LR(1) and LALR(1) tables and compare the power of LR(0), SLR, LALR and CLR parsers.
topics: Relative power of LR parser classes

nodes.name: Precedence parsing
nodes.desc: Operator precedence and associativity in grammars, operator-precedence parsing and yacc.
nodes.summary: You will be able to encode operator precedence and associativity in grammars and parse with operator-precedence parsers and yacc.

nodes.name: Syntax-directed
nodes.desc: Syntax-directed definitions and translation schemes, and evaluating them on a parse tree.
nodes.summary: You will be able to write syntax-directed definitions and translation schemes and evaluate them on a parse tree.

nodes.name: Attribute grammars
nodes.desc: Synthesised and inherited attributes, S-attributed and L-attributed definitions.
nodes.summary: You will be able to distinguish synthesised and inherited attributes and classify definitions as S-attributed or L-attributed.

nodes.name: Translation schemes
nodes.desc: Embedding actions in grammars, infix to postfix translation and evaluation order.
nodes.summary: You will be able to embed semantic actions in grammars, translate infix to postfix and work out the order actions run in.
topics: Position of actions and output order

nodes.name: Semantic checks
nodes.desc: Type checking and the semantic errors a compiler detects.
nodes.summary: You will be able to describe how a compiler performs type checking and which semantic errors it detects.

nodes.name: Intermediate code
nodes.desc: Syntax trees, DAGs and three-address code as intermediate representations.
nodes.summary: You will be able to represent programs as syntax trees, DAGs and three-address code and compare these intermediate representations.

nodes.name: Three-address code
nodes.desc: Quadruples and triples, SSA form, and translating expressions and array references.
nodes.summary: You will be able to translate expressions and array references into three-address code and store it as quadruples, triples or SSA.

nodes.name: Code generation
nodes.desc: Instruction selection, register allocation and the minimum registers an expression needs.
nodes.summary: You will be able to describe instruction selection and register allocation and compute the minimum registers an expression needs.
topics: Minimum registers for an expression tree

nodes.name: Runtime environments
nodes.desc: Static, stack and heap allocation, and how storage is organised at run time.
nodes.summary: You will be able to explain static, stack and heap allocation and how storage is organised at run time.

nodes.name: Activation records
nodes.desc: Activation records and trees, access links and displays for nested procedures.
nodes.summary: You will be able to describe activation records and trees and explain how access links and displays reach non-local variables.

nodes.name: Scoping & parameters
nodes.desc: Static versus dynamic scoping, and call by value, reference, value-result and name.
nodes.summary: You will be able to trace programs under static and dynamic scoping and under call by value, reference, value-result and name.

nodes.name: Code optimisation
nodes.desc: Machine-independent optimisation on basic blocks and control-flow graphs.
nodes.summary: You will be able to apply machine-independent optimisations on basic blocks and control-flow graphs without changing program meaning.

nodes.name: Local optimisations
nodes.desc: Common subexpressions with DAGs, constant folding, strength reduction, dead code and loop-invariant motion.
nodes.summary: You will be able to apply common subexpression elimination with DAGs, constant folding, strength reduction, dead code removal and loop-invariant motion.
topics: DAG construction for a basic block

nodes.name: Data-flow analysis
nodes.desc: Basic blocks, control-flow graphs, liveness and other data-flow analyses.
nodes.summary: You will be able to perform liveness and other data-flow analyses over control-flow graphs.
